_about: Every Slither finding on contracts/src (active contracts: HonorCatPots, MultisigResolver, PasskeyAccount, PasskeyAccountFactory), reviewed. CI (slither-gate.py) fails on any finding not listed here. Keys are the detector plus the finding's first line with source locations removed.

findings.key: arbitrary-send-eth: PasskeyAccount.execute(address,uint256,bytes,uint64,WebAuthn.WebAuthnAuth) sends eth to arbitrary user
findings.reason: Intended: execute is the account owner's generic call. It runs only after a WebAuthn signature by the account's passkey over (chainId, account, nonce, target, value, dataHash, deadline), verified on-chain; the nonce prevents replay.
Same call as above; a generic account must use a low-level call. The success flag is checked and the revert data is bubbled up.
The target is chosen and signed by the passkey owner; a call to address(0) only wastes the owner's own transaction and moves nothing it did not sign.

findings.key: uninitialized-local: MultisigResolver.isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes).last is a local variable never initialized
findings.reason: False positive: starts at address(0) on purpose so the first recovered signer passes the strictly-increasing check.
The clone address is computed beforehand with predictDeterministicAddress and is the same value; the call reverts if deployment fails.

findings.key: unused-return: MultisigResolver.isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes) ignores return value by (signer,err,None) = ECDSA.tryRecover(digest,sig)
findings.reason: Only the third value (the raw signature-s error detail) is ignored; signer and err are both checked.
The call is to the freshly deployed clone's initialize; the event order has no security effect.
Signature deadline (minutes); drift cannot extend it meaningfully.

Not exploitable: every flagged function is nonReentrant, the only external calls are to Arc USDC (a trusted ERC-20) through _pay/_pull, and positions are minted/moved with _mint/_transfer (no receiver callback). State that matters (pot state, escrows, deposits) is updated before the transfers; the flagged writes after a call are to already-settled fields.

Intended: block timestamps are the protocol's clock (exit and join windows, lock-out before trading close, attestation timeouts, deadlines). Arc has deterministic sub-second finality; a validator cannot move time by minutes, and every window has seconds-to-minutes granularity.

Intended: _pay uses a low-level transfer so a failed payment (e.g. a blocklisted recipient) becomes a claimable balance instead of reverting the whole settlement. The return data is checked.

Intended: block.timestamp is the protocol clock. The reader refuses a quote window that has not ended yet or ended more than maxAge seconds ago; a validator's few seconds of timestamp drift only shifts that freshness bound slightly and cannot forge a price (the window is signed by the pot's signer set).
